## Construction and represented cases

`ownerSelection` scans constructor registration labels, reads indexed formals, selects computation formals at the exact target owner, reads unique registration recipes, and requires exactly one candidate at the planned root component. Missing/duplicate recipes of eligible constructors fail rather than being skipped. Function/entry equality does not choose the owner. `sourceProbe` computes every probe field from R55 primitive indexed/unique reads. `incidence` checks exact R45 OwnerReads/Identity plus the actual native parameter-recipe equation, which R45 alone did not contain. The complete concrete permission vector is retained.

`readRoot` checks source incidence/artifact/entry first, then reads the selected emission, lower effect lane/current physical bound, indexed admission, bound/readback agreement, slot uniqueness, admission relation and exact relation endpoints, and finally the unique completed source-drain root. `BeforeAncestry` is the exact R47 Matches conjunction with only the ancestry conjunct removed; the final certificate rechecks all of those guards. The reader uses only the input physical emission index; it reads the stored emission/admission itself.

`root_current_slot`, `root_source_fields` and `root_native_projection` give the current bound, unique slot event, origin/cause/task/completion and exact source FactId projections on this same native. `complete_after_ancestry` reinserts the existing R47 ancestry guard. The existing R61 ordered visitor handles all seven dependency projections and both Replay parents without replacing or changing any theorem body.

`source_failure_precedes_ancestry` and `ancestry_failure_precedes_outer_identity` prove the exact critical order retained by R58 policy. Later entries retain their existing directed root ancestry; Catch keeps its existing policy branch. The finite primitive R57 fixture computes both a receipt and successful first entry. Checked rejection equations cover missing/duplicate permissions, duplicate constructors, swapped target owner, foreign use, missing/duplicate roots, stale current storage, wrong physical owner, wrong drain cause/incompletion, and failed ancestry before an outer admission identity mismatch. These are kernel computations over fixture inventories, not claims about Rust reachability.
